arms.better: tm found the relevant Path implementation and typing patterns, but repeatedly reread the same source and spent 1,100,017 reported input tokens across two failed attempts without producing a patch. Both attempts ended with the CLI's generic ‘something went wrong: model ended turn without submitting’ and only suggested rerunning the same ticket; a user would have little indication whether their code, configuration, or prompt needed attention, and retrying did not help. A more explicit plan, a targeted no-submit recovery path that inspects or continues the saved attempt instead of repeating it unchanged, and clearer failure copy would make this workflow substantially more useful. The overwritten PR regression tests mechanically failed: the Path test module had 1 failure/7 passes/1 skip because Path was not generic at runtime, and mypy reported 11 typing errors.

OpenCode stated a scoped three-step plan, found the Path generic and conversion methods quickly, implemented the typing change, and reported focused tests and both available checkers accurately; its own typing test and the merged PR tests passed. It also identified that ty was unavailable rather than claiming it ran. It could be more efficient by discovering the repository's canonical typing-test layout sooner and extending tests in the dedicated typing_path.py file rather than typing_prompt.py; nevertheless, the independently restored PR tests verified the implementation successfully.
